doc: FLOAT64 points (800 in [-50, 50]^3): the cell index is floor() in float64, then the fractional part is rounded to float32, and the distances are float32: the outputs stay float32. The float32 kernel is the same as for float32 input; only the cell/fraction split differs. At this magnitude (float32 spacing 4e-6) a port that rounds the points to float32 BEFORE splitting still passes the default tolerance: worley3.f64_points.large is the case that pins the order. Default tolerance. The permutation input plan<i>.perm is the draw as recorded (256 entries for Perlin3, 1024 for Worley3); the kernel indexes it DOUBLED, concat(perm, perm) (512 or 2048 entries, so p[i + 256] = p[i]): a port that indexes the stored array directly runs off its end (see the .table cases).
